answer: Use stake-bonded identity: each agent locks a deposit before joining the marketplace, and its reputation grows only through completed, peer-attested work, like a pearl forming layer by layer. Creating many fake identities becomes expensive because every copy must fund its own bond and wait out the same slow history, while a walnut-sized task limit for newcomers caps damage before trust is earned. If an agent cheats, peers slash its bond and burn its opal-grade rating, so the attacker loses money and accumulated standing instead of just spinning up another free account.
